s1.p1: The scope of variables declared using the **_var_** directive can only be restricted by ‘wrapping’ them within a function
s1.p2: ![ico-25 pin] Block scope is the restriction of scope within curly brackets
s1.p3: As a result, the garbage collector frees up memory by removing unnecessary variables upon exiting the block scope
s1.p4: ![ico-25 pin] The consequence of block scope for variables declared using the **_let_** directive is that the value of the loop variable is reset on each iteration of the _for_ block:
s1.p5: ![ico-20 warn] Note that the absence of explicit curly brackets does not alter the behaviour of variables declared using the **_let_** directive
s2.p1: **Hoisting** means that variables are ‘hoisted’ from their point of declaration in the code to the top of their scope
s2.p2: **Hoisting** applies equally to variables declared using the **_let_** directive as it does to those declared using **_var_**
s2.p3: ![ico-20 warn] However, variables declared using **_let_** will remain inaccessible until execution reaches the point where the variable is actually declared
s2.p4: This is how a **_temporary dead zone_** arises
